title: It did not come from an observatory.
description:
It did not come from an observatory. The planet was found at Lowell Observatory in Arizona. The name was suggested at a breakfast table in Oxford, England.

The discovery was announced on 13 March 1930. The next morning, 14 March, Falconer Madan of the Bodleian Library read the story in The Times and mentioned it to his granddaughter.

Venetia Burney's age when she suggested the name Pluto for the new planet.

Granddad told an astronomer. Madan passed her suggestion to Herbert Hall Turner, an astronomer and a friend of his.

Turner cabled it to Lowell Observatory. As reported by Mental Floss and Today I Found Out, it read: 'Naming new planet, please consider PLUTO, suggested by small girl Venetia Burney for dark and gloomy planet.'

Her grandfather rewarded her with five pounds for the name.

Eleven years old. Five pounds. A world named.
